extracted.intended_audience: general readers and media/technology industry observers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and expectations for how news organizations should use, disclose, and oversee artificial-intelligence-produced or -assisted reporting, and how they should attribute authorship and correct errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and transparency as core journalistic values
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism builds and markets its values-based products around the notions of truth and transparency; if you want to be in the truth-telling business, you shouldn’t tell lies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat secrecy about production methods as a form of lying; prioritize honest disclosures about how stories are produced. (Quote from Tom Rosenstiel: “A secret is a form of lying.”)

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of AI’s role in story creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit when artificial intelligence or technology assisted in or created a story (e.g., notes at the end of AP stories explaining technology’s role).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear statements that technology was used and in what capacity rather than leaving that information implicit or hidden; the AP example places a note at the end specifying technology and data providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not attribute work to nonexistent or fake reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid publishing articles under bylines of authors who cannot be identified or who appear to be fabricated (e.g., author photos that are AI-generated portraits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate author identities and remove or correct content that uses fake personas; the Futurism investigation found author profiles linked to AI-generated portraits and prompted content removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent, not buried, disclosure of AI involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures about AI involvement should be clear and easily discoverable, not hidden behind clickable author attributions or obscure links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t require readers to click through to learn that AI played a role (CNET’s initial approach hid the information behind 'CNET Money Staff' attribution); place disclosures where readers will readily see them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between AI-native and AI-enhanced content
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate content that is 'AI-native' (created by AI in ways not possible without it) from content that is 'enhanced by AI but created by humans' and label accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt labels or bylines that communicate the extent and nature of AI involvement (e.g., Buzzfeed credited 'Buzzy the Robot' alongside a human writer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vet and hold third-party content providers accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: When outsourcing content creation to third parties, publishers must verify claims that content was written and edited by humans and take responsibility for misrepresentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct due diligence on vendors (Sports Illustrated said AdVon Commerce assured them content was human-written); remove content and end partnerships if assurances prove false while investigating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and quality control for AI experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain rigorous editorial oversight, fact-checking, and quality control when experimenting with AI-generated content to avoid errors and reputational damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn from past failures (Gannett and CNET experienced errors) and pause or adjust experiments when errors occur; ensure human review processes are in place before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct errors transparently and update readers
rubrics_metrics.description: If machine-generated content contains errors or the use of AI was undisclosed, publish corrections and clarify production methods to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After discovery of problems, publicly acknowledge mistakes, issue corrections, and make future disclosures clearer (CNET corrected stories and later made AI usage more explicit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit technology and data providers used in production
rubrics_metrics.description: When technology or datasets contribute materially to a published story, identify and credit the providers (e.g., AP noting technology from Data Skrive and data from Sportradar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include brief statements in articles describing which technologies or data sources were used and how they contributed to the reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to basic journalistic standards when using AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to fundamental newsroom ethics and standards — including accurate bylines, transparency, and honest reporting — even when adopting new technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unions and newsroom stakeholders demand adherence to basic standards, explicitly opposing publishing 'computer-written stories by fake people'; organizations should codify AI policies that align with journalistic ethics.
